vocabulary.meaning_en: to take something from someone and give it back later
vocabulary.example: May I borrow your pen?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give something to someone for a short time
vocabulary.example: I can lend you my book.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to lend (verb, mostly US); money or a thing that is lent (noun)
vocabulary.example: I loaned my stapler to a friend.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give something back
vocabulary.example: Please return the book on Monday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to return something to where it came from
vocabulary.example: I'll bring them back tomorrow.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where you buy and eat meals
vocabulary.example: We are meeting at a restaurant tonight.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to do something special for a happy day
vocabulary.example: We celebrate my birthday with a cake.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the day of the year you were born
vocabulary.example: Today is my sister's birthday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the money you get from your job, usually as a check
vocabulary.example: I get my paycheck every two weeks.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you give to someone; a present
vocabulary.example: Thank you for the gift!

vocabulary.meaning_en: two, or a small number
vocabulary.example: I need a couple of things from the store.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool that joins papers with small metal pieces
vocabulary.example: Can I use your stapler?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool with two blades for cutting paper
vocabulary.note_ar: دائماً جمع: these scissors, a pair of scissors.
vocabulary.note_en: Always plural: these scissors, a pair of scissors.
vocabulary.example: These scissors are very sharp.

vocabulary.meaning_en: able to cut easily
vocabulary.example: Be careful. The knife is sharp.

vocabulary.meaning_en: giving attention so you don't make mistakes or get hurt
vocabulary.example: Be careful when you cross the street.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to believe that someone is honest and will do the right thing
vocabulary.example: You can trust me.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to annoy or interrupt someone
vocabulary.example: Sorry to bother you, but can I ask a question?

vocabulary.meaning_en: things used in an office: pens, paper, tape and so on
vocabulary.example: We need more office supplies.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to let someone use something that is yours too
vocabulary.example: My brother and I share a room.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a sticky strip used to hold things together
vocabulary.example: Fix the paper with tape.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small thing used to remove pencil marks
vocabulary.example: Can I use your eraser?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thin ring of rubber to hold things together
vocabulary.example: Put a rubber band around the cards.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small bent wire to hold papers together
vocabulary.example: Use a paper clip, not the stapler.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thin rubber bag filled with air
vocabulary.example: The children love balloons.

vocabulary.meaning_en: unusual and makes you want to know more
vocabulary.note_ar: أحياناً تُقال بتردد لتعني «غريب» بلطف، كما فعلت Marsha.
vocabulary.note_en: Said slowly, it can be a polite way to say "strange", as Marsha does.
vocabulary.example: That is an interesting idea.

fine_lines.title: borrow vs lend
fine_lines.explanation_ar: borrow = تأخذ شيئاً من شخص لفترة (أنت تستلم). lend = تعطي شيئاً لشخص لفترة (أنت تعطي). نقول: May I borrow your stapler? و I can lend you my stapler. لا نقول: Can you borrow me...
fine_lines.explanation_en: Borrow = you take something for a short time. Lend = you give something for a short time. Say "May I borrow your stapler?" and "I can lend you my stapler." Don't say "Can you borrow me...".

examples.sentence: I can lend them to you.
I borrowed a pen from Anna.

fine_lines.title: lend vs loan
fine_lines.explanation_ar: loan كفعل تعني lend (في الإنجليزية الأمريكية). وكاسم: a loan = قرض (مال تقترضه من البنك).
fine_lines.explanation_en: As a verb, loan means lend (mostly American English). As a noun, a loan is money you borrow, often from a bank.

examples.sentence: I loaned my stapler to the wrong person.
Could you lend me your eraser?
He got a loan from the bank.

expressions.phrase: Have a nice day at work!
expressions.meaning_ar: أتمنى لك يوماً جميلاً في العمل!
expressions.meaning_en: A kind goodbye in the morning.
expressions.example: Have a nice day at work, Dad!

expressions.phrase: Do you have a pen I can borrow?
expressions.meaning_en: Asking to use someone's pen for a short time.
expressions.example: Do you have a pen I can borrow? Mine is broken.
Can I sit here? - Of course.

expressions.meaning_en: Asking if someone did not remember.
expressions.example: We had a meeting today. Did you forget?

expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to ask to use something.
expressions.example: May I borrow your phone charger?

expressions.meaning_en: I will do the right thing.
expressions.example: I'll bring it back tomorrow. You can trust me.
Thanks for your help! - Don't mention it.

expressions.meaning_en: Said before asking someone who is busy for something.
expressions.example: Sorry to bother you, but where is the bathroom?
Thanks for the books. I'll bring them back tomorrow.

expressions.meaning_en: Asking about the use of something.

grammar.title: Asking permission: May I / Can I + verb?
grammar.explanation_ar: لطلب الإذن نستخدم May I + الفعل (أكثر رسمية وأدباً) أو Can I + الفعل (عادية وشائعة). بعدهما الفعل في المصدر. الرد بالموافقة: Sure. / Of course. / Yes, you can.
grammar.explanation_en: To ask for permission use May I + base verb (more formal and polite) or Can I + base verb (normal, common). Answers: Sure. / Of course. / Yes, you can.
examples: May I sit here? - Of course.

grammar.title: borrow something / lend someone something
grammar.explanation_ar: borrow + الشيء (+ from + الشخص): I borrowed a pen from Amelia. lend + الشخص + الشيء أو lend + الشيء + to + الشخص: She lent me a pen / She lent a pen to me. ومع ضمير المفعول نستخدم to: I can lend them to you.
grammar.explanation_en: Borrow + thing (+ from + person): I borrowed a pen from Amelia. Lend + person + thing, or lend + thing + to + person: She lent me a pen / She lent a pen to me. With a pronoun object use to: I can lend them to you.
examples: I can lend you my stapler.
I can lend them to you.
I'll just have to borrow a couple of things.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: Can you borrow me your pen?
questions.explanation_ar: أنت تأخذ الشيء، فنستخدم borrow: Can I borrow your pen?
questions.explanation_en: You are taking it, so use borrow: Can I borrow your pen?

questions.question: Complete: "Sure. I can ____ you my stapler."
questions.explanation_ar: المتكلم هو الذي يعطي الدبّاسة، فنستخدم lend.
questions.explanation_en: The speaker gives the stapler, so use lend.

questions.question: Which request is the most formal and polite?
questions.explanation_en: May I... is the most formal and polite.

questions.question: Someone says "Thank you." A good reply is ...
questions.explanation_ar: Don't mention it = لا شكر على واجب.
questions.explanation_en: "Don't mention it" is a reply to thank you.
